outcome.reason: Customer lost job and has no current income. Unable to pay at this time, will reach out if situation improves.

transcript.text:
Good afternoon! This is Mumbai Bank calling regarding your overdue credit card payment. I wanted to remind you that your outstanding balance is currently overdue, and a late fee of ₹1,500 has also been applied. Non-payment can significantly affect your credit score and may even lead to legal action.

Could you please let me know when you will be able to clear your dues? If you’re facing any difficulty in making the payment, I’m here to help—please let me know your situation.
Good afternoon. I understand, but I lost my job three weeks ago and I don’t have any income right now. I really can’t pay anything at the moment.

I’m really sorry to hear about your situation. Mumbai Bank understands that tough times can happen. To support you, I can offer a waiver on a portion of your outstanding dues—up to 50%—to help reduce your burden. This will lower both your overall amount payable and your late fees.

Would you be able to pay if we provided this discount? If not, we can discuss a payment plan that suits your current situation. Please note that continued non-payment will further impact your credit score.

What amount would you be comfortable paying right now if we offer a 50% waiver?
I appreciate the offer, but honestly, I don’t have any money right now to pay anything at all. I’m just trying to get by until I find a new job.

Thank you for sharing your situation honestly. We truly want to support you. Since you’re unable to pay right now, I can note your hardship and update your account accordingly. However, I must inform you that as long as the outstanding amount remains unpaid, late fees and interest (around 12% per year) will continue to accrue, and your credit score will be affected. This could make it harder to get loans or credit in the future.

Would you like me to schedule a follow-up call in a few weeks to check your situation again? That way, we can discuss payment options when things are a bit better for you. Please let me know a suitable time frame for a callback.
I’m not sure when things will get better. I can’t really say a time frame right now. Maybe sometime next month, but I can’t promise anything.

I understand it’s difficult to commit right now, and I appreciate your honesty. I’ll make a note in our system not to pressure you further at this time. However, please remember your account will continue to accrue interest and late fees, and your credit score will be affected.

If your situation changes or you need assistance with payment options or waivers in the future, feel free to contact Mumbai Bank. Also, if you become eligible and need funds later, we have a festive loan offer at 9.5% interest rate which could help with short-term needs.

For now, I’ll check back with you next month to see if your circumstances have improved, unless you’d like a different arrangement.

Thank you for your time today. We wish you the best, and hope things improve soon.
Thank you for understanding. I appreciate you not pressing me right now. I’ll try to reach out if things change. Have a good day.
